His mind wouldn’t settle. Thoughts spun. He allowed himself to slide back to the floor, leaning his back against the wall. Even if She had decided to reward his efforts somewhat, the healing he sorely needed wasn’t coming back. Not really. Not enough. Something was stacking in his blood — something meant to be flushed, purged, burned out. Uroboros used to handle it. It didn’t anymore. The toxins stayed. Something hissed low in his throat. Not quite a cough, just a sound pulled tight through fraying nerves. His hand flexed against the cuff. The strength was still there, somewhere — he could feel it, buried under the static — but it wasn’t answering. Every movement came with delay. Every twitch rebounded wrong. He wasn’t lagging. He was decaying. In the stillness, something shifted. The quiet sound of pen on paper wafted, distant and crisp through the overhead intercom. Shh-sskt. Shh-sskt. Scribble. Pause. Scribble again. Wesker’s jaw locked. Not a word. Not even a taunt. Just notes being taken. As if he were already dead, and this was just postmortem data collection. The cuff hissed lightly, a warm numbness carrying swiftly up his arm, making the lights smear. He squeezed his eyes shut against it, trying to dodge the nausea and instead finding fatigue in its place. For once, he welcomed it, letting his mind slip past seared nerves. For once, the cuff didn’t punish the drop. The intercom clicked off with a small pop. Chapter 11 – Control Group The Fog opened on tile and steel. Dim lights buzzed overhead. The R.P.D. was quiet — too quiet. Wesker hit the ground running, boots pounding down familiar corridors. The station pressed around him, claustrophobic, boxing him in. Every scrape of his coat against the wall felt amplified, every echo biting. His impromptu rest the previous day had dulled the edge but didn’t fix the rot. His coordination had sharpened, but not his rhythm. His strength returned in furtive bursts of controlled violence, then collapse. The cuff hadn't sparked once since waking, but he could feel it waiting. And someone was watching him again. Gabriel. Obvious. Deliberate. The man vaulted late, body-blocked narrow corridors, backtracked into rooms already cleared, loitered in view instead of working on the generators. Wesker's lip curled. The others scattered and played smart — but not him. It was like the pest wanted to get caught. Wesker ignored the obvious bait for a while, refocusing on breaking generators, on sending survivors scattering away with his blade, on keeping upright and moving. But Gabriel wouldn’t stop. Again and again, he pulled attention back, always just close enough to force Wesker’s hand. It worked. Gabriel clipped a doorframe as he rounded a corner. Wesker surged behind him, one arm lashing out, a hand catching his collar mid-sprint and slamming him with full momentum into the wall. Tile cracked. A filing cabinet toppled. Wesker loomed over him, fury etched into every line of his face. The gloved palm locked just under Gabriel’s collarbone, holding him there with pressure that bordered on crushing. Gabriel wheezed under the force, both hands locked around his arms like he could pull Wesker away. A mildly wet undertone to the inhales told him that he likely broke the man’s ribs on impact. Good. He wanted to observe so badly? This is what he got. Wesker’s breath shook. Every heartbeat sent a spike through his limbs — static-slick and heavy. The toxins were stacking again. But he didn’t move. He wanted Gabriel to see it. The glow of the cuff shimmered along the killer's wrist, flickering with the rhythm of an overworked pulse. Gabriel’s eyes tracked it immediately. Closer now. Too close. He could see the faint shadow of a line running along the side, and the way the red light throbbed like a warning. There it is. Wesker followed his gaze and snarled. “You think you’re clever? Curious little rat. You and your pathetic group, following me around like I’m some kind of sideshow... Is this what you were after? Is this a close enough look for you? You think staring it is going to make it vanish?!” The cuff flared in warning. Pain lanced up his arm. His muscles locked mid-hold, nerves sizzling. His grip spasmed for half a breath — and then he tightened it. Not today. Gabriel braced for worse — and got it. Wesker pulled Gabriel sharply to the side before letting his tremors finally loosen his grip, the momentum sending him flying through the glass of a nearby window. Shards rained down over Gabriel as he crumpled to the small office floor coughing and writhing. Wesker sidestepped the weak attempts at kicking him away to grab a fistful of coat again, hauling Gabriel off the ground and marching him out of the office. The cuff flared hotter against him, another chemical wash joining the current in an attempt to throw him off target, but he moved quickly through it to slam Gabriel back first into a hook. He barely managed a single yelp before the Entity’s claws were on and through him, greedily hauling her snack away to be rebuilt back at the campfire. Wesker dragged his breath through clenched teeth, watching the body vanish into light. The cuff went silent again. But Wesker’s blood wouldn’t stop ringing. The exit gates groaned open, locks grinding free as alarms wailed. Survivors scattered, shouts carrying through the Fog. Wesker staggered toward back rooms of the station, rather than follow them for a possible last- minute catch, every spark from the cuff kicking through his frame like a whip. His breath rasped, echoing harshly through the silence. His stride faltered, weaving unevenly into the ruined halls. Jake lingered behind, grinning through his bruises. He loved a dramatic finish — a final loop, a wink
